items.title: Scalar partial differential operators, order, and classical solutions
Linear, semilinear, quasilinear, and fully nonlinear partial differential equations
Principal part and principal symbol of a scalar PDE
The principal symbol depends only on the first derivative of a smooth coordinate change
items.strategy: Expand repeated derivatives of a pulled-back unknown under a smooth local diffeomorphism, isolate the terms in which every differentiation lands on the unknown, and recognize every term involving higher derivatives of the coordinate map as lower order.

items.title: Characteristic covectors, hypersurfaces, and noncharacteristic data
Characteristic hypersurfaces are independent of the defining function
items.strategy: Replace one defining function by a nonvanishing multiple, compute the new conormal on the zero set, and use the homogeneity of the principal symbol to show that the characteristic condition is unchanged.

items.title: Elliptic, hyperbolic, and parabolic principal symbols
A symmetric second-order principal part has a coordinate-invariant signature normal form
items.strategy: Freeze the coefficients at a point, interpret the principal quadratic form as a self-adjoint operator, diagonalize it orthogonally, and use Sylvester's law to see that only the signature survives further linear coordinate changes.

items.title: The discriminant for a second-order equation in two variables
In two variables, type and characteristic directions are coordinate invariant
items.strategy: Transform the principal quadratic form by the Jacobian matrix, observe that the discriminant picks up the square of the Jacobian determinant, and identify characteristic directions with the tangent directions annihilated by the pulled-back principal symbol.

items.title: Constant-coefficient second-order equations in two variables have canonical principal forms
items.strategy: Use the discriminant and signature classification of the constant symmetric coefficient matrix to choose a linear change of variables that diagonalizes the principal part, then rescale to the Laplace, wave, or rank-one parabolic normal form.

items.title: Limits of the elliptic-parabolic-hyperbolic trichotomy
Linear transport equations and their characteristic flow
A transport equation restricts to a linear ODE along each characteristic
items.strategy: Differentiate the composite t mapsto u(X(t), t) by the multivariable chain rule and substitute the characteristic ODE.

items.title: Transport characteristics depend C^1 on the initial position
items.strategy: Write the characteristic equation as a Volterra integral equation, estimate difference quotients by continuous dependence and Gronwall, and pass to the limit to obtain the Jacobian matrix solving the linearized system.

items.title: Homogeneous linear transport is solved by the inverse characteristic flow
items.strategy: Along each in-domain characteristic, the transported quantity is constant, giving the inverse-flow representation and uniqueness. Conversely, flow consistency and the chain rule recover the PDE directly from any C1 function satisfying that formula.

items.title: The inhomogeneous linear transport equation has the characteristic integrating-factor formula
items.strategy: Restrict a PDE solution to each in-domain characteristic and apply the scalar integrating-factor theorem. Conversely, use flow consistency to identify the displayed formula with that scalar ODE solution and apply the chain rule to recover the PDE.

items.title: Noncharacteristic Cauchy surfaces for first-order transport
Local linear transport has a unique solution from noncharacteristic Cauchy data
items.strategy: Build the jointly C1 space-time flow from the data surface, use transversality and the inverse function theorem to obtain characteristic coordinates, solve the scalar linear ODE along each characteristic, and pull the result back to prove existence and uniqueness.

items.title: Support propagates along transport characteristics
items.strategy: In the homogeneous formula, the solution at time t is the initial datum pulled back by the inverse flow, so it vanishes exactly away from the flow image of the initial support.

items.title: Characteristics are covectors before they are curves

title: Partial Differential Equations and Characteristics — Examples

items.title: Constant-velocity transport translates the initial profile
items.strategy: Solve the characteristic ODE explicitly as straight lines and substitute the inverse translation into the homogeneous transport formula.

items.title: Transport with growth and source along straight characteristics
items.strategy: Use the inhomogeneous characteristic formula with explicit integrating factor and straight-line characteristics to compute the solution and then verify the PDE directly.

items.title: The stationary equation x dot Du = u is solved by radial characteristics
items.strategy: Follow rays x(s) = e^s x_0 away from the origin, observe that u satisfies u prime = u along them, and rewrite the result in polar form.

items.title: Characteristic Cauchy data may be nonunique or incompatible
items.strategy: Choose a data curve that is itself characteristic. Constant data along that curve do not determine a unique nearby solution, while nonconstant data violate the compatibility relation and admit no classical solution.

items.title: Laplace, heat, and wave equations have elliptic, parabolic, and hyperbolic principal symbols
items.strategy: Extract the principal part of each model operator and compute the corresponding quadratic symbol or time polynomial to read off its type.

items.title: A constant-coefficient hyperbolic equation is diagonalized by characteristic coordinates
items.strategy: Factor the principal quadratic form into two real characteristic directions, use those directions as new coordinates, and rescale the remaining coefficient to the standard wave form.

items.title: The Tricomi equation changes type across y = 0
items.strategy: Compute the discriminant of y u_xx + u_yy and read its sign separately on y greater than 0, y less than 0, and y = 0.

items.title: The elliptic-parabolic-hyperbolic trichotomy is not a global taxonomy
items.strategy: Combine the Tricomi operator, which changes type from point to point, with a fourth-order operator whose principal part lies outside the scalar second-order trichotomy.
